The cost of one unit, and the cost per thousand

Source: R/units.R
cost_per_unit.Rd

Derived from planned_spend and planned_units, never stored separately, so neither can disagree with the plan's money.

Usage

cost_per_unit(plan)

cpm(plan)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

Value

A numeric vector, one per row of @data. NA where a row records no units.

Details

cost_per_unit() is always the price of a single unit. cpm() is the trade's cost per thousand — the figure actually quoted for impressions — and is simply cost_per_unit() * 1000, reported for any unit type on the assumption that you asked for a reason.

Examples

p <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(channel = c("Social", "Search"),
             unit_type = c("impression", "click"),
             planned_spend = c(140000, 95000),
             planned_units = c(28000000, 118750)),
  grain = "channel", name = "Q3 plan"
)

cost_per_unit(p)
#> [1] 0.005 0.800
cpm(p)
#> [1]   5 800
p@data$planned_rate      # the CPM for Social, the CPC for Search
#> [1] 5.0 0.8
